title: Muscles That Deflect Whips
text: “Ah, well, yeah… how should I put it… it’s the opening show where we whip Shion and the others, the one we’d actually abolished once already. But Shion and the others got so ridiculously buff that when Elena-san does the whipping, it just ends up looking fake.”

Look, Father said, pointing at Lazy Pig and the Crocodile Guys getting whipped. And indeed, that was true. Perhaps because of how bulging the Crocodile Guys’ muscles had become, every lash just seemed to bounce right off their defenses. They were putting on a show of looking like they were in pain, and the whip was rigged with fake blood to redden the skin, but there were hardly any actual welts, so anyone with sharp eyes would surely grow suspicious.

“Yeah. Theo, for instance—when he did the demonstration in his beastman form, his fur just blocked everything and only got a little discolored red. So now, even when he switches to his demi-human form for the actual show, the whipping barely does any damage anymore. And Wolf, well, he’s a Hero, so…”
Rabbit Guy had been left tough on purpose, what with the important job of being kicked by Filo-tan being entrusted to him. That was clearly the cause here.

“You really are putting on quite the farce,” Itsuki said. “The act itself makes me sick, but… since it’s presented as deception, I suppose I can find it amusing. If you’re not going to commit fully to the lie, then there’s no fun in it for me.”
Itsuki seemed as much a misanthrope as ever.
“Should we buff Lazy Pig, then?”
“I did have Elena-san level up too, but the growth rate for those three… I bumped up their growth rate and intentionally kept their levels low to fake it, but we’ve hit a wall.”

It seemed like it was only a matter of time before the whole thing got exposed as a total sham. Hmm… Father seemed to be mulling it over. Were the Crocodile Guys really that attached to this particular act? I could understand it being some kind of reward, getting whipped personally by Father. And beyond that, it was a act where they got to be the main attraction, so I supposed there was some fondness for it too.

“The one who kept warning me is putting on quite the serious performance of really laying into them,” Itsuki said. “He’s been practicing pretty diligently at taking whippings. Maybe we need to raise the attack power of the one doing the whipping.”
Originally, Father’s policy had been to cut this act down, but apparently without it, they couldn’t draw crowds in Melromarc, so it had stuck around.
“It’d probably be best to have Shion and the others step down from this act, but that alone would make them unhappy, so I’d need to find them another act to join.”
“What a troublesome business… well, I can offer plenty of advice regarding whipping, but they’re already fairly used to it themselves.”
“Yeah… both Theo and Shion have plenty of experience with it, after all.”
“If we’re keeping this act, then who would even be a suitable replacement to take charge of it…”

“Speaking of which, Itsuki, could you please stop burning the faces of people clapping and laughing from the bottom of their hearts into your memory with murderous eyes? It’s terrifying—like you’re going to go kill them in the middle of the night.”
“Ha ha ha. You noticed, did you.”
“…Please tell me that’s a joke? Because if you actually do it, I’m the one who’s going to get suspected.”
Father seemed to be having quite a bit of trouble handling Itsuki. Just how far were you going to keep troubling Father, I wondered?
“Bhoiii! Bhoi bhoi!”

Hm? Lazy Pig raised both hands and made some kind of declaration, and then the monster dealer’s underlings brought baskets full of stones out into the audience seats, selling them to the crowd. Those who claimed to have some skill with throwing snatched them up and hurled them at the Crocodile Guys. Thud, thud—the thrown stones struck the Crocodile Guys one after another.
“Elena-san really worked that improv well… well, I did prepare those stones originally for Keel-kun and the others’ act anyway.”
“The ‘everyone throw stones’ bit, huh. Truly stomach-turning. Mind if I kill them all?”

Ugh… the memory of that loop where I’d pushed Father to his absolute limit came rushing back, and I nearly threw up blood from my stomach. Ah, Father from that loop, I am truly sorry. Someday, I shall atone for my sins… though I wonder if I ever really could.
“Destroy them, I say.”
A sudden urge to atone for my sins welled up within me, so perhaps rampaging alongside Itsuki wasn’t such a bad idea after all.
“No, we’re not doing that.”
“The rot in people who’d take joy in an act like this ought to be exterminated. Wouldn’t destroying them be for the good of the world?”
“Motoyasu-kun, I get, but Itsuki, your whole line of thinking has started sounding like a final boss from some story.”
Aren’t there plenty of villains in stories who preach genocide in the name of ‘for the good of the world’? Father said. Indeed, I felt like I’d seen something similar back when I was in Japan.

“Even so, I think that’d be fine. Well… if we want to play it safe, then perhaps Naofumi-san handles support and buffs while Motoyasu-san and I apply debuffs to the slaves? That should work well enough as is.”
“Ah, I see… yeah, that’d probably be the safest option. Shion and the others have decent resistance to debuffs, but if Itsuki goes all out, it shouldn’t be impossible to land them.”

Father was skilled at support. Though he hadn’t yet gone to Cal Mira Island, he could likely learn magic to raise attack power, and if he properly buffed Lazy Pig beforehand, the act could go exactly as originally intended.
“I’ll run a test later. Itsuki, want to help me out?”
“I’d rather not cooperate much, but since it’s become a nuisance, fine.”
“Father, am I no good for this?”
“If Motoyasu-kun can cast debuffs, sure, why not?”
“I have no aptitude for it, but I can manage indirectly, I say. Come to think of it, doesn’t Itsuki also lack aptitude for this?”
If I recalled correctly, the magic Itsuki learned on Cal Mira Island was the opposite of Father’s Aura—something called Down—but Itsuki’s own natural aptitude should have been Wind and Earth.
“It’s outside my jurisdiction too, but ability-down type spells were easier for me to pick up through elemental magic, as it happens.”
“Ren apparently has an aptitude for support, but it should be the ‘up’ type… well, all we really need is enough defense-down to have Shion and the others take a bit of damage.”

That’s right, Ren did have an aptitude for support. Hmm… now that I thought about it, I couldn’t picture Father casting ability-down type spells at all. Perhaps being good at raising things meant being bad at lowering them. No… actually, once Father had learned Aura on Cal Mira Island, he probably figured that was good enough and left it at that. Down-type spells, admittedly, tended to land poorly if the target resisted. And it was also true that Itsuki’s Down spells were particularly powerful in that regard. And so, while proposing various improvements, we watched the show together. Thus the first act came to an end, and one after another, the show moved on to the next acts. Incidentally, while the opening acts leaned toward abuse, Father had programmed it so that the later in the show you got, the more the acts required humans and demi-humans to work together in harmony. And so, the next act was knife-throwing performed by Panda.
“Fwaah… guess it’s my turn.”

Panda, with one eye marked with a star pattern and dressed in a clown costume, walked past us. Ever since joining the circus, Panda had spent most of her time looking utterly listless, but when it came time to actually work, she had a stance of doing what needed doing. Come to think of it, wasn’t Panda napping around the circus grounds about as much as Lazy Pig these days? Or so I thought, but apparently it was because Father used the resting Panda as a sort of healing-mascot backrest while he worked. Slipping past the watchful eyes of her grandfather and adoptive father to laze about had apparently become a habit for her. Of course, she was forced to accompany her grandfather in training every single day without fail. Outside of that, though, she wanted nothing more than to rest.
“Lars-chan. Good luck out there.”
“I never fail, y’know.”

As if it were now just another part of daily life, Panda gave a light wave and lumbered off. And the ones tied to the target changed daily among the slaves. Sometimes even Keel performed in this role. Once out on stage, Panda had been instructed not to speak, so she appealed to the audience purely through gestures. With the spotlight on her, she did forward rolls and backflips before standing in the center of the venue with her arms spread wide, and meanwhile, a large target with a slave tied to it was carried in from behind. Today… it looked like it was one of Panda’s own underlings performing. Panda would then climb atop an even larger ball, wobbling precariously while throwing her knives.
